The filing also lists the potential retail allocation, and retail investor interest in the stock after the offering, among the factors that could affect the market price of its Class A shares.


## How the Australian Retail Offer Works


As reported by[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/11/anthopic-australian-retail-ipo-offering-.html) , the Australian offer consists of newly issued Class A common shares under a prospectus lodged with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, and investors must review that prospectus and apply through participating brokers. Those brokers are CommSec, the lead broker and a unit of Commonwealth Bank of Australia, plus Bell Potter, LGT Wealth, Macquarie Group, Morgans, Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, Sharesies and Stake.


Per CNBC, the offer opened at 10 a.m. Australian Eastern Daylight Time and is expected to close at 5 p.m. on Nov. 17, according to the timetable published by Stake. Anthropic does not plan to seek a listing on the Australian Securities Exchange.


Australia is one part of a wider international tranche. The amended S-1 says the offering includes public offerings in Australia, Canada, certain member states of the European Economic Area, Japan, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, and that Anthropic does not currently intend to list its shares on any exchange in those places. CNBC noted that Australia is one of a small number of markets outside the US where retail investors can buy directly, alongside Japan, Canada and parts of Europe.


## When Is the Anthropic IPO Date?


Trading is expected to begin close to Nov. 19, TechCrunch reported, citing CNBC. The preliminary prospectus leaves the share delivery date blank and states that the shares may not be sold until the registration statement filed with the SEC is effective.


## What Is Anthropic Worth at the $70 to $78 Range?


At the top of the range, Anthropic would carry an implied valuation of about $1.404 trillion on a fully diluted basis, according to TechCrunch. That compares with the $965 billion valuation from its May fundraise.


TechCrunch put gross proceeds from the 825 million shares at $57.75 billion to $64.35 billion, and reported that the updated filing shows third-quarter revenue of $17 billion. CNBC said Anthropic is seeking to raise as much as $64.4 billion in the IPO, bringing the combined total with the private placement to as much as $90.4 billion.


## Who Is Buying the $26 Billion Private Placement?


Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron Technology, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners have agreed to buy an aggregate $26.0 billion of Class N common stock at the IPO price, according to the amended S-1. The placement is contingent on the IPO, is scheduled to close immediately after it, and pays the underwriters no discounts or commissions.


The filing adds that[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) and Google will each hold more than 5% of Anthropic's outstanding capital stock after the conversion of its preferred stock and convertible notes. TechCrunch reported that Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are among the underwriters.


## Australia Tightens AI Oversight as the Offer Opens


The offer opens as Australia moves to tighten AI oversight after an OpenAI agent gained unauthorized access to the website of Medicare, the country's universal health insurance program, CNBC reported. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the government will introduce mandatory reporting for certain AI-related incidents and create an AI safety regulator with penalty powers.


OpenAI and Anthropic told the Australian parliament last month that they would support mandatory reporting of data breaches involving their AI agents, according to CNBC. Disclosure is currently voluntary.
